title: Reorg Headcount Phantom: Position Alive in Adaptive but Eliminated in Workday
scenario:
**Workday HCM — Position Management (as of June 15, 2026)**
Position ID: P-04217 | Title: Senior Compliance Analyst | Sup Org: Risk & Compliance — Wealth Mgmt | Cost Center: CC-4420 | Status: Closed — Eliminated | Effective Date: April 1, 2026 | Incumbent at closure: Marcus Tate (termed 3/31/2026) | Reason: Reorganization

**Adaptive Planning — FY26 Workforce Model (exported June 20, 2026)**
CC-4420 (Risk & Compliance — WM): Planned HC = 18 | Filled = 16 | Open = 2
Open positions listed: P-04217 (Sr. Compliance Analyst), P-04301 (Compliance Manager)
Budgeted comp for P-04217: $142,000 base + 15% target bonus
Last model refresh: March 28, 2026 (pre-reorg sync)

**ServiceNow HR — Case HRTASK0019843 (April 14, 2026)**
Requester: Diane Kowalski (VP, Risk & Compliance)
Subject: "Backfill for Marcus's role"
Description: "Need to open a req for the senior compliance analyst seat. Marcus's last day was 3/31. The wealth management integration work still needs coverage."
Assigned to: Talent Acquisition | Status: In Progress
TA Comment (April 16): "Opened REQ-2287 — titled 'Compliance Integration Specialist' per Diane's updated JD."

**Microsoft Teams — #wm-leadership (April 2, 2026, 8:47 AM)**
@diane.kowalski: Quick update — the reorg is official as of yesterday. Marcus's position was eliminated per the restructuring plan. I'm going to submit a new role under a different title that better reflects what we actually need.
@greg.fontaine: Makes sense. Same band?
@diane.kowalski: Bumping it to B5 since we're adding the integration scope. Already talked to Devon about it.
@greg.fontaine: 👍
[No further replies]

**SharePoint — /hr-ops/reorg-tracker-Q2-2026.xlsx (last modified April 3, 2026)**
Row 34: P-04217 | Action: Eliminate | Effective: 4/1/2026 | Savings realized: YES | Finance notified: YES
Row 35: [no entry for replacement role]

**Dynamics 365 — Vendor invoice (May 2026)**
Vendor: Korn Ferry | Description: Executive search — Compliance Integration Specialist, Wealth Mgmt | PO: linked to CC-4420 | Amount: $38,500 (first installment)
question: Finance is flagging CC-4420 as over-planned by 1 FTE because Adaptive shows 2 open positions but only 1 open req exists in Workday. What is the correct current state of headcount for CC-4420, and what action resolves the discrepancy?
choices: A) CC-4420 has 0 net new open positions because the elimination savings were already realized; the new role should be on a different cost center
B) The discrepancy cannot be resolved until Diane formally submits a new position creation through the position management workflow in Workday
C) CC-4420 has 1 open position (REQ-2287/new role); Adaptive needs a manual sync to remove the eliminated P-04217 and add the new position at B5
D) Adaptive is correct (2 open); Workday needs P-04217 reopened since a backfill was approved
rationale: The Adaptive Planning model last synced on March 28 — three days before the reorg effective date of April 1. This means Adaptive still shows P-04217 as open when it was actually eliminated. Meanwhile, a new role (Compliance Integration Specialist at B5) was created through ServiceNow HR and is being actively recruited for via Korn Ferry, but it exists under a different title and band than the eliminated position. The correct state is 1 open position (the new role), not 2. The fix is a manual Adaptive sync that removes the phantom P-04217 and adds the new position. Answer A is wrong because P-04217 was intentionally eliminated — the new role is a distinct position, not a reopening. Answer A is wrong because the Teams conversation and ServiceNow case confirm the new role is approved and budgeted to CC-4420 (the Korn Ferry invoice proves it). Answer D is wrong because the position creation already happened via the ServiceNow workflow and TA opened the req; the issue is purely a sync failure in the planning tool, not a missing approval.

**Microsoft Teams — #hris-integration (February 12, 2026, 3:22 PM)**
@devon.washington: Heads up — the Piedmont sup org migration is done in Workday as of 1/15 but Adaptive won't pick it up until the next scheduled sync (first week of March). Until then, Tom Whitfield will still show as cost center owner in any planning reports.

**Outlook — Email (March 22, 2026)**
From: thomas.whitfield@cascadefinancial.com

Subject: RE: Year-end rating delegation
> Tom — can you confirm you're no longer the reviewer for the East advisory team?

Devon — I still have 'approve' access in the old PFS performance module that hasn't been decommissioned. I haven't used it since January but technically I could still submit ratings. Should I flag this to compliance?

**Dynamics 365 — Contact Record: Priya Venkatesh**
Reports To: Thomas Whitfield | Department: PFS-Advisory | Last Modified: November 2025
question: It is now June 2026. An auditor asks: in how many systems does Priya Venkatesh currently report to the wrong manager, and what is the compliance risk?
choices: A) Two systems (Adaptive Planning and Dynamics 365); moderate risk because cost center ownership affects budget approval routing
B) Three systems (Dynamics 365, Adaptive Planning, and SharePoint org chart); moderate risk requiring cleanup but no immediate compliance exposure
C) Two systems (Dynamics 365 and the legacy PFS performance module); material compliance risk because an unauthorized individual retains rating approval access
D) One system (Dynamics 365 only); low risk since CRM reporting lines don't affect compensation or performance decisions
rationale: By June 2026, the ServiceNow case from March confirmed that Adaptive Planning was updated (resolution on March 10 states the mapping was fixed). The compliance risk is material because an individual who is no longer the manager retains the technical ability to submit performance ratings — this is a segregation-of-duties issue that could affect compensation decisions. Answer A misses the PFS performance module entirely (the critical signal buried in Whitfield's email). Answer C includes SharePoint, but a stale PowerPoint labeled 'Draft' is not a system-of-record with workflow impact — it's a presentation artifact. Answer D incorrectly includes Adaptive (which was fixed in March per the ServiceNow resolution) and misses the performance module risk entirely.

title: WARN Act Trigger Date: Which System's Termination Is Authoritative?
scenario:
**Workday HCM — Termination Report (RIF Wave 2, June 2026)**
Filter: Cost Center CC-3200 (Retail Banking Ops — Southeast) | Termination Reason: Position Elimination
22 workers terminated | Effective dates range: June 28–30, 2026
Notable: 3 workers show effective date of June 30 but 'last day worked' field is blank

**SharePoint — /legal/rif-planning/wave2-WARN-analysis.docx (last modified June 10, 2026)**
Section 2: "WARN threshold analysis — Southeast region"
"Current planned separations for 90-day lookback window (April 1 – June 30): 47 total across CC-3200 and CC-3210. Threshold is 50 for single site. Recommend proceeding — sufficient margin."
Section 3: "Assumptions: Termination date = Workday effective date. Voluntary resignations excluded."

**ServiceNow HR — Cases filed week of June 16, 2026**
HRTASK0021200: Employee Jordan Miles (CC-3200) | Subject: "Requesting earlier separation date" | Description: "Jordan has accepted a new role starting June 16. Requesting term date moved from 6/30 to 6/13 to allow clean transition." | Approved by: HRBP Lisa Morton | Status: Closed
HRTASK0021215: Employee Anita Pham (CC-3210) | Subject: "Extending through July for project handoff" | Description: "Anita's manager requesting extension to July 15." | Status: Pending VP approval
HRTASK0021222: Employee David Roark (CC-3200) | Subject: "Separation agreement dispute" | Description: "David's attorney counter-signed agreement with July 5 effective date. Legal reviewing." | Status: In Progress

**Microsoft Teams — #hr-legal-rif (June 18, 2026, 11:03 AM)**
@lisa.morton: Devon — Jordan Miles's term date got moved up to 6/13 per his request. Already updated in Workday. Does that pull him into the prior lookback window?
@devon.washington: If his effective date is now 6/13, he falls into the April-June 13 window instead of April-June 30. Need to check if that changes the count for the earlier period.
@lisa.morton: The earlier period had 28 separations. Adding Jordan makes 29. Still under 50.
@devon.washington: Right but double check — is his separation 'voluntary' since he requested the acceleration? Or still coded as RIF?
@lisa.morton: Good question. I left the reason code as position elimination since that's the original basis. He just moved the date up.
@devon.washington: 🚨 That matters. If he's counted as involuntary in the earlier window, recount everything.
[Thread continues below]
@lisa.morton: Recounted. April 1–June 13 window: 31 involuntary (including Jordan). Still under.

**Outlook — Email (June 20, 2026, 4:45 PM)**
From: outside.counsel@barrettlaw.com
To: legal-rif@cascadefinancial.com
CC: devon.washington@cascadefinancial.com
Subject: RE: Roark separation — effective date
"Confirming David Roark's separation agreement is now fully executed with an effective date of June 30, 2026. Note: the agreement contains a 5-day revocation period, meaning the earliest irrevocable date is July 5. For WARN counting purposes, we recommend using the irrevocable date."

**Adaptive Planning — Headcount Forecast (June 2026 snapshot)**
CC-3210: Shows Anita Pham as 'active' through July 15 (extension assumed approved)
CC-3200: Shows 22 terms on June 30 (does not reflect Jordan's accelerated date or Roark's revocation-period adjustment)
question: Using outside counsel's recommended counting methodology, how many involuntary separations fall within the 90-day lookback window ending June 30, 2026, and does Cascade trigger WARN Act notification requirements for the Southeast site?
choices: A) 47 separations; does not trigger WARN (under 50 threshold)
B) 46 separations; does not trigger WARN — Jordan's acceleration moves him out of the June 30 window, and Roark's irrevocable date of July 5 moves him out as well
C) 48 separations; does not trigger WARN (under 50 threshold) — subtract Jordan (moved to earlier window) and Roark (moved to July), but add Anita's extension keeps her in the window
D) 45 separations; does not trigger WARN — Jordan moves to the earlier window, Roark moves to July 5 window, and Anita's extension to July 15 removes her from the June 30 count
rationale: The WARN analysis requires precise date attribution using the authoritative methodology (outside counsel recommends irrevocable date). Starting from the original 47 in the April 1–June 30 window: (1) Jordan Miles's effective date moved to June 13, but Lisa confirmed in Teams he still counts as involuntary — however, his accelerated date means he falls into a lookback window ending June 13, not June 30. For the window ending June 30 (April 1–June 30), Jordan at 6/13 IS still within the window, so he remains. Wait — re-reading: the original 47 was across CC-3200 AND CC-3210. Jordan was already counted in the 47. Moving his date to 6/13 doesn't remove him from the April 1–June 30 window since June 13 is within that range. The real adjustments are: Roark's irrevocable date is July 5 (per counsel), removing him from the June 30 window (-1 = 46). Anita Pham's extension to July 15 means her separation is no longer in the June 30 window (-1 = 45). Jordan remains in the window (June 13 is between April 1 and June 30). Final count: 45. Answer A uses the stale SharePoint analysis without any adjustments. Answer B correctly removes Roark but incorrectly removes Jordan (June 13 is still within the April 1–June 30 window). Answer C invents an addition for Anita when her extension actually removes her. The critical insight from outside counsel's email is that the revocation period shifts Roark's counting date to July 5.
